rationale: The Shed Cam shows RSSI -87 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections and choppy live view. The customer confirmed a 25m distance with a kitchen wall and a newly installed metal fence in the signal path, and the standard fix (moving the camera closer) made it stream perfectly, confirming the camera itself is fine and the cause is weak signal/attenuation. All other devices are online, ruling out a system-level fault.

repair_steps: Confirm the Shed Cam is back in its original location and still showing RSSI below -80 dBm.
Recommend installing the official RP-1 repeater between the house and the shed to bridge the 25m gap and bypass the metal fence.
If the customer prefers not to use a repeater, suggest relocating the base station to a window facing the garden or moving the camera closer to the house.
After the customer implements a solution, verify the RSSI is above -80 dBm and the camera remains stable for at least 24 hours.
Close the case as resolved at frontline.

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.
